title: Member Accounting Memo: Shortfall Allowance on Payment Arrangements Installments by Member Standing
content:
**Member accounting memo — Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements): shortfall allowance**

**Rule.** The shortfall allowance deducted when an installment is tested as missed follows the member's standing:

- where the agreement carries no earlier missed-installment entry and the member's Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) account in the patron class of the service account's rate schedule has been open at least 300 calendar months on the day the miss is recorded, $20.00 is deducted;
- where the agreement carries no earlier missed-installment entry and that capital credit account has been open fewer than 300 months, or the member holds none, $10.00 is deducted;
- where the agreement already carries a missed-installment entry, nothing is deducted.

**Records read.** The earlier missed-installment entries are those already on the agreement's ledger. The capital credit account is the member's Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) account in the patron class into which the service account's rate schedule allocates patronage; its months open are counted in calendar months from its opened date to the day the miss is recorded. 300 calendar months are twenty-five years.

| Earlier missed-installment entry on the agreement | Capital credit account in the patron class | Months open on the day | Allowance deducted |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | held | 300 or more | $20.00 |
| none | held | 299 or fewer | $10.00 |
| none | none held | — | $10.00 |
| one or more | any | any | nothing |

**Hypothetical members:** a household whose Residential Patron Class account was opened 312 months before the day the miss is recorded receives $20.00 on the first miss of its agreement and nothing on a second; a member whose account in that class was opened 120 months before receives $10.00 on the first miss.
